before: Ruby interpreter and gem versions are different. Gem::Version compares version components, and Gem::Requirement checks a declared requirement. The constraint >= 6.0, < 7.0 admits compatible-major candidates, not proof that every API or application behavior works.

require loads an available library; a Gemfile and reviewed lockfile describe a reproducible application dependency resolution when using Bundler. This example only evaluates local version requirements: it installs nothing and makes no network request. Native extensions and platform compatibility need separate checks.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
require "rubygems"
requirement = Gem::Requirement.new(">= 6.0", "< 7.0")
puts requirement.satisfied_by?(Gem::Version.new("6.0.0"))

```
Expected output or behavior: true. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why recording only RUBY_VERSION cannot reproduce all gem dependencies. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

Accept a version at least 6.0 and below 7.0.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
require "rubygems"
requirement = Gem::Requirement.new(">= 6.0", "< 7.0")
puts requirement.satisfied_by?(Gem::Version.new("6.0.0"))
```
The output is `true`. Version 6.0.0 fits. The check does not install a gem.
